edits.title: Reuse fetched evidence across single and batched research
edits.content: When research mixes single and batched fetching, retain successful fetched text in a URL-keyed dictionary. Deduplicate candidate URLs while preserving order and exclude URLs already cached before calling fetch_many. Associate returned pages with their input URLs, retain usable results, and build extraction evidence directly from the cache. Reuse those same cached strings to check that each extracted citation refers to a supplied URL and contains a verbatim quote. A cache read demonstrates local evidence reuse; it does not establish a backend cache hit. Exercise both single and batched calls only when required or useful for the task.

additional_candidates.description: Deduplicate fetch targets and reuse URL-keyed fetched evidence for extraction and citation validation.

decisions.reason: The self-check reports empty output, and its citation and coverage arrays are empty despite successful constraint-call records. The final visible root block places refine.run before answer assignment, but the snapshot contains neither that block's completion nor a submission result. Extraction did produce five rows with no reported validation failures. There is no demonstrated recovery or sufficient evidence to attribute the empty output to an agent failure rather than snapshot timing; the immutable instructions already require serialization and readiness assignment.

Both flagged queries returned four hits and recorded no new entities after the single search had recorded all five requested quantities. The user explicitly required batched search for this demonstration. The results supplied table sources subsequently fetched and used for extraction, so neither occurrence establishes an unproductive search loop. No recovery or search-policy change is warranted.

The fetch block deduplicated batch URLs, excluded the singly fetched URL, stored four pages by URL, and reread cached text. The extraction used that evidence, and subsequent checks reported five rows with no quote/source or domain failures. Fetch records show four successful backend fetches, supporting local reuse without implying a backend cache hit. This is a reusable intermediate procedure; final submission success remains unverified. No existing entries require updating.
